question.text: Ravi has Rs.10 lakh to invest. He puts Rs.3 lakh in equity funds, Rs.4 lakh in debt funds, Rs.2 lakh in gold ETF, and Rs.1 lakh in a liquid fund. What percentage of his portfolio is in growth-oriented assets?

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook treats equity as a growth-oriented asset class and describes physical assets such as gold, including Gold ETFs that track domestic gold prices, as growth investments as well. Counting both equity (Rs.3 lakh) and gold ETF (Rs.2 lakh) as growth assets gives Rs.5 lakh out of the Rs.10 lakh portfolio, which is 50%. The Trap: Counting only equity gives 30% and skips gold's growth classification. 70% and 40% do not correspond to any consistent grouping of the four holdings under the workbook's growth-versus-income framing. Note: The growth classification of equity and gold (including Gold ETFs that track domestic gold prices) is taken from the workbook. The workbook does not state that a 50% growth allocation is the appropriate fit for a moderate risk appetite, so that suitability claim is not part of this explanation.
